title: Separate a screenshot's text into layers you can move, with nothing left behind
goal: Take a screenshot, right click the picture, choose Separate into Layers, and every run of text in it becomes its own layer you can pick up and move. Where a word came from, the background is filled with what was around it, so dragging a label off a dark button leaves the button looking untouched rather than punching a hole in it. Anything the app cannot read confidently is left in the picture and not mentioned.
notes:
The foundation slice. The user said "I'd love this to at least work on text runs", so this one alone has to be worth having on its own: text out, nothing left behind, one undo.

Scope discipline: no boxes, no hierarchy, no shadows here. Those are the sibling tasks and they depend on this. What this slice owes them is the seam: a sweep that returns pieces, a patch step, and a builder that turns pieces into layers in one undo step. Design those three so the next slice adds a detector and a nesting pass without reopening any of it.

---
SHARED CONTEXT for the Separate into Layers set (asked for by the user on 2026-09-12).

The user's words: "Often I take a screenshot and want to layerize the pieces, so that i can move them around. I wish there was a way to intelligently layerize the parts of the ux. A label, a text run, a box. If there's text in a box, I wish they were heirarchically organize in the layers. I would love somewhere to be an auto layerize feature, but i don't know where. maybe right click on a layer (or the bg layer) and select 'Auto separate'? ... If there is text in a black bg, when we layerize the text, the layer behind it should fill the containing area with the best interpolated color match. If we are layerizing a box, we fill the hole underneath it so that moving the box layer doesn't create a hole. There are some edge cases like shadows. If we can extract that as an actual shadow effect that can move with the layer, that would be amazing. But in the worst case we ignore parts that we can't interpret. I'd love this to at least work on text runs, but ideally break things up so i can easily move the parts individually."

Three things the user was explicit about, which are acceptance criteria and not nice-to-haves:
1. NO HOLES. Taking a piece out and moving it must never reveal a gap. What was behind it is filled with the best match the surrounding pixels can justify.
2. HIERARCHY. Text inside a box comes out as a child of that box, not as a sibling in a flat pile.
3. IGNORE WHAT YOU CANNOT READ. A part the app cannot interpret is left in the background picture, untouched and unmentioned in the layer tree. Guessing badly is worse than skipping.

THE BIG REUSE, read this before designing anything. The measure tool already finds UI elements in a screenshot and already computes the nesting this feature needs:
- PhotonzRender/EdgeMapAnalyzer.swift:36, analyze(CGImage) -> EdgeMap, builds the edge map from a bitmap.
- PhotonzCore/ElementBounds.swift:117, candidates(at:in:luma:...) returns "the nested ladder of element rects around point, innermost first, each containing the one before it", and its own doc comment describes climbing from a line of text to its row to its card. That ladder IS the hierarchy the user is asking for, already written and already tested.
- TextLineBounds finds a line of text geometrically, with a gap parameter for what ends a line, and ElementBounds already has a rule (captionHeightRatio at ElementBounds.swift:113) for when words belong to the control wearing them rather than being an element of their own. That rule is exactly the text-in-a-box question.
- LumaField carries brightness.
The gap between what exists and what this needs is NOT detection. It is: sweeping the whole picture instead of probing one point, cutting a piece out, PATCHING what was behind it, and building the group tree.

Do not reach for Vision or OCR in the first slices. The geometric detectors above already find text lines and boxes with no new dependency, and the app has no Vision usage at all today. Vision's VNRecognizeTextRequest becomes the right tool only for the later slice that turns a run of text into an editable text layer, because that needs the actual characters. Say in the audit how well the geometric pass did before adding a dependency.

THE PATCH, which is the genuinely new machinery and the thing most likely to be done badly. Note first that promoteRegionToLayer (PhotonzCore/Document.swift:741) COPIES a region into a new layer and leaves the original underneath untouched: it has never cut a hole, which is why moving a promoted piece today reveals the same pixels still sitting there. Recommended approach, in this order, and the runner should justify what it chose:
- Sample a ring of pixels just outside the piece being removed. If it is near uniform, fill with that one colour. This is the overwhelmingly common case in real UI: words on a solid button, a bar, a card.
- If the ring varies along one axis, fit a linear gradient to it and fill with that.
- Otherwise extend the nearest border pixels inward.
Do NOT attempt content-aware inpainting. On flat UI it is unnecessary, and on a photograph it would invent detail that is not there. Where even the fallback would be a visible guess, SKIP the piece per rule 3 rather than smearing the picture.
WHERE THE REPAIR GOES, corrected by the user on 2026-09-12 after reading an earlier draft of this task: "if i separate text from a box, i know it doesn't affect the layer underneath, I mean that I WANT it to fill that space with the bg color so that the text is on one layer the bg is on the other". So the result is exactly TWO things and not three: the piece on its own layer, and the background layer with the space it came from filled in. Do NOT stack a separate repair layer above an untouched original - that was the earlier plan here and the user rejected it, because it leaves you with a tree that does not match the simple thing you asked for.

That means the background layer's own pixels are repaired, which is a bake rather than a render-time effect. It is still fully undoable and that is the requirement, not non-destructiveness: undo is a whole-document snapshot, the original bitmap stays in ImageStore, and one Command-Z brings the untouched screenshot back. The app already bakes pixels deliberately in exactly this way - Rasterize Layer, and Turn a shape into a picture - so this is a precedent being followed, not the non-destructive rule in CLAUDE.md being broken. Note in the design doc that this is the one place the app repairs a picture in place, and why.

WHERE IT LIVES. The user's instinct is right: the right-click menu on a layer row, which already exists (Sources/Photonz/LayersRow.swift:202, .contextMenu). It also belongs in the Layer menu, where every other layer command lives (Sources/Photonz/EditorCommands.swift:368). It has to be offered on the background picture layer, which is the case the user actually starts from. The user suggested calling it "Auto separate"; "Separate into Layers" says the same thing in the app's own plainer voice. Pick one, use it in both places, and ask the user in the audit rather than shipping two names.

Everything else: one Separate is ONE undo step however many layers it produces (History.perform, CLAUDE.md). The separated layers get names a person can read in the list, not "Promoted Layer" repeated eleven times. Queue-driven app work targets the NEXT release, and a Current change is not finished until Next has it.

Design doc: docs/design/separate-into-layers.md is the source of truth, written by the foundation task and extended by the rest.
acceptance: The command is reachable by right clicking a layer row and from the Layer menu, both offered on the background picture layer, under one name used in both places
Running it on a real screenshot puts each run of text on its own layer, named so the layers list is readable
Moving a separated run reveals a filled background, not a hole: sample the pixels where the word was and show they match what surrounds them, in the audit, with numbers rather than by eye
The uniform case is exact: white words on a solid dark bar leave that bar one flat colour where the words were
A run the app cannot read confidently is left in the background picture and produces no layer, and the audit shows a case where that happened
The result is two layers and not three: the text on its own layer and the background with the space filled in, with no extra repair layer in the tree
The whole thing is one undo step: one Command-Z puts the screenshot back exactly as it was, whatever it produced
Running it twice on the same layer does not separate the same text again or stack a second repair
Tests: the sweep and the patch decision are covered in PhotonzCore and PhotonzRender against a real fixture capture, written before the implementation
A playtest walk runs the command on a fixture screenshot and drags a separated run clear of where it came from
Perf note in the commit: how long the sweep takes on a 12 megapixel capture, measured
docs/design/separate-into-layers.md written: the sweep, the patch rules and their order, what is deliberately skipped, and how the later slices extend it
Audit under queue/audits/ with before and after captures, a magnified patch, and anything rough filed as a follow-up
